items.summary: Tinashe’s eighth album is her best and bravest yet: more ambitious, more focused, and effortlessly in touch with the zeitgeist. It’s the best pop album of the year.

items.title: Westside Whimsy
items.summary: After records steeped in grief and heartbreak, the singer’s latest album is framed as a laid-back ode to Los Angeles, but it can be tough to tease out the substance behind the sunny vibes.

items.title: Intentions
items.summary: On her International Anthem debut, the Los Angeles-based singer threads R&B, jazz, and downbeat electronic into lovestruck reveries that still feel true to life.

items.title: Dream House
items.summary: Lorely Rodriguez’s fifth album contends with the grief of losing her childhood home in a wildfire. These songs still center her virtuosic voice, but sometimes smother her eccentric perspective.

items.summary: On her fourth album, the Australian singer-songwriter surrenders to the idea of change, filling her warm, reassuring songs with poignant imagery and a greater sense of perspective.

items.title: Nearly
items.summary: Saying more with reverb and echo than with words, the London producer’s new album gives the impression of ECM jazz records collaged into effortless sophisti-pop ballads.

items.title: Mule
items.summary: The South African-born country singer’s latest album is a hell-and-back tale of addiction and redemption. But where other artists might opt for austerity, Peck goes all in on his usual pomp.

items.title: Paddywhackery
items.summary: Righteous sociopolitical furor sounds timeless and accessible on the sextet’s third album, which combines Irish trad with rock and punk to interrogate history, identity, and class struggle.

items.title: Northern Exposure
items.summary: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the British DJs’ monumental 1996 mix, a virtuosic blend of after-hours grooves and floor-filling intensity that helped to canonize the elusive sound of progressive house.
